result: The authors developed and optimized a combined tissue expansion (C-MAP) and tiling light-sheet microscopy (TLSM) protocol for planarians, achieving up to 4.5-fold linear expansion, imaging resolutions of 120-500 nm, and rapid whole-organism imaging within 1-12 hours depending on resolution.
evaluation: All three reviewers explicitly praised this methodological development. The editor noted it 'represents a substantial improvement on current standards and enables more rapid data acquisition.' Reviewer 1 stated 'the resulting workflow can produce highly detailed and quantifiable 3D reconstructions at a rate that is fast enough to allow the analysis of large numbers of whole animals.' Reviewer 2 called it 'a useful method' and praised 'high-quality images that show the utility of this technique.'

result: The authors developed an automatic 3D cell segmentation pipeline and applied it to quantitatively profile neurons and muscle fibers at the single-cell level in over 400 planarians, using five neuron markers (cholinergic, serotonergic, octopaminergic, GABAergic, and dopaminergic) that label most neurons throughout the body.
evaluation: Reviewers consistently praised the segmentation methodology. Reviewer 2 noted 'their analysis pipeline permits them to quantify cell types in relatively large numbers of whole animal samples.' The editor emphasized this as demonstrating 'the utility of this solid protocol.' Reviewer 1 acknowledged the workflow allows 'quantification of neurons, muscle fibers, and all cells in individual worms,' though noted uncertainty about sub-cellular resolution performance.

result: The study validated several previous observations including neuronal cell number changes, muscle fiber distribution, photoreceptor axon projections (both ipsilateral and contralateral), glial-photoreceptor associations, and the four-layer body-wall musculature structure.
evaluation: Reviewer 2 explicitly stated 'Many of their findings confirm previous results in the literature, which helps validate the techniques and pipelines they have applied here.' The editor noted the work demonstrates utility by 'quantifying several aspects of this flatworm's neural anatomy and musculature.' These validation findings were treated as confirmatory evidence supporting the methodology rather than novel discoveries.

result: During homeostasis, neurons increase proportionally with body size up to ~7mm, comprising ~10% of total cells, but beyond this threshold the neuron-to-cell ratio decreases, potentially due to allometric growth or relating to fission. Different neuron subtypes and brain regions show distinct growth patterns.
evaluation: Reviewer 2 stated 'The authors provide convincing data on changes in total neurons and neuronal sub-types in different-sized planaria.' The findings were described as consistent with previous reports, with Reviewer 2 noting the work provides 'additional evidence, obtained through comprehensive analyses of entire animals at the single-cellular level and in greater sample sizes.' No concerns were raised about these quantitative homeostasis findings.

result: During regeneration, different neuron populations exhibit distinct temporal dynamics: cholinergic and serotonergic neurons increase continuously throughout 14 days, while GABAergic, octopaminergic, and dopaminergic neurons appear around days 3-4 and plateau after day 10, with regional patterning emerging by day 4.
evaluation: Reviewer 2 noted the authors 'provide convincing data' on neuronal changes and that findings 'confirm previous results in the literature, which helps validate the techniques.' The temporal dynamics were treated as well-supported by the comprehensive single-cell level analysis across 251 samples. The editor's summary acknowledged the work quantifies aspects 'during homeostasis and regeneration' without raising concerns.

result: High-resolution imaging revealed distinct muscle distribution patterns at anterior and posterior poles, with circular fibers dominating dorsally, diagonal and longitudinal fibers more prominent ventrally at the tail, and dorsal-ventral (DV) fibers making close contact with other fiber types.
evaluation: Reviewer 2 explicitly stated 'They report differences in body wall muscle pattern between the anterior and posterior poles of the planaria' as a strength of the work. The high-resolution observations of muscle fiber organization and contacts were enabled by the 120 nm imaging capability, which reviewers acknowledged as demonstrating the utility of the technique.

result: In β-catenin-1 RNAi planarians, both anterior and posterior muscle fibers resemble the cobweb-like structure normally found only anteriorly, and there are more longitudinal fibers in dorsal regions, suggesting a correlation between muscle structure and anterior-posterior axis establishment.
evaluation: Reviewer 2 specifically highlighted this as a new observation and strength: 'that these differences are lost when a posterior head forms in beta-catenin RNAi planaria' and 'show that the muscle pattern in the posterior head of beta-catenin RNAi worms resembles the anterior muscle pattern.' This finding was treated as convincing evidence linking muscle organization to body axis patterning.

result: Glial cells extend from the CNS to body-wall muscle fibers and show tight associations with dorsal-ventral muscle fibers in the epidermis region, and neurons are closely associated with muscle fibers through their projections.
evaluation: These observations of glial-muscle and neuron-muscle associations were acknowledged by reviewers as part of the study's comprehensive characterization. Reviewer 2 noted the work demonstrates 'the potential of the approaches they are taking' through such detailed cellular interactions. The high-resolution imaging capability enabling these observations was consistently praised.

result: In inr-1 RNAi planarians, there are disruptions in neural-muscular networks including locomotion defects, altered body proportions, increased circular muscle fibers, fewer cholinergic neurons, disordered GABAergic neuron distribution, and altered glial cell morphology with reduced projections to muscles.
evaluation: Reviewer 2 stated 'They also find that glial cell projections are reduced in insulin receptor-1 RNAi planaria' as a strength and new observation. The comprehensive characterization of inr-1 RNAi phenotypes across multiple cell types was enabled by the quantitative imaging approach that reviewers praised. No concerns were raised about these findings.

result: The study discovered previously unreported muscle-muscle and neuron-muscle connections, including DV fibers connecting body-wall muscles to pharynx, and close spatial correlation between newly regenerating muscle fibers and cholinergic neurons, suggesting muscle may guide nervous system regeneration.
evaluation: Reviewer 2 acknowledged these as among the 'new observations' and strengths of the work. The editor noted the study demonstrates utility by revealing such cellular interactions. While the interpretation that 'muscle may guide nervous system regeneration' is somewhat speculative, reviewers did not challenge this interpretation and it follows logically from the spatial-temporal correlations observed.

result: The evidence suggests muscle fibers serve as a scaffold for targeted neuron projection and may play a crucial role in guiding regeneration of the planarian nervous system.
evaluation: While Reviewer 2 acknowledged the observations of muscle-neuron associations as new findings, this interpretive claim about muscle serving as a 'scaffold' and 'guiding' regeneration represents a mechanistic inference. Reviewer 1 noted 'it is unclear how well their technique as described will perform at sub-cellular resolutions,' which relates to the level of detail needed to definitively establish scaffolding relationships. The spatial correlations support but do not prove the proposed guidance mechanism.

result: The current resolution for segmentation may be limited when resolving fibers within densely packed regions of the nerve tracts.
evaluation: Reviewer 1 directly raised this concern, stating 'it is unclear how well their technique as described will perform at sub-cellular resolutions based upon the data that they show.' This limitation was acknowledged by the authors themselves in the manuscript, and reviewers confirmed it as a valid constraint of the current methodology.
